answer: Creating N fake identities costs N bonds plus the opportunity cost of idle capital, so a swarm attack scales linearly in expense while honest agents recover their stake. A practical sybil defense is staking-weighted identity: each agent locks a bond to register, and reputation accrues only through verified interactions tracked on a single thread of signed attestations. Like an oasis rewarding travelers who cross the desert, the protocol pays persistent contributors at each dawn, and any identity that fails peer checks loses its bond, making mass fabrication economically irrational.
